new_results.statement: For scalar pivot a and Schur complement S, each pair polynomial star H_q equals a times the off-diagonal Schur row, det B_q=a S_qq, and sum_q ||H_q||^2=a^2(||S||_F^2-sum_q S_qq^2). Exact zero stars on all nonnegative pairs isolate every same-sign Schur coordinate.

With one literal hub, one leaf square lambda vv^T plus physical diagonal, mixed Gram G and leverage <=1/2, ||p_Q||_infinity <=3*2^(4/3)(|lambda| det G)^(-1/3), with continuous density and the same linear interval coefficient.

The two-parameter Walsh family Q_{delta,epsilon} has det B=delta and partner polynomial star norm 4 epsilon, is target-valid for all delta in [0,1], epsilon>=0, yet pinned mixed-hub smoothing gives ||p_Q||_infinity<=3 uniformly while the partner pair-star bound is 6.4709493274 epsilon^(-1/2).

partner_result_applied.application: On Q_{delta,epsilon}, H=4 epsilon d, so for epsilon>0 the full-law partner bound is ||p_Q||_infinity<=6.470949327404231 epsilon^(-1/2). The comparison with the uniform mixed-frame constant 3 proves that target validity cannot force the pair-star currency at universal scale.

pinned_result_applied.application: Condition literal X_2; retain X_1 as hub and Y as product leaves. Dense same-side ww^T remains active, star is 4c, G=diag(1,16), leverage 2/m<=1/4, hence |phi(t)|<=pi^(3/2)|t|^(-3/2), ||p_Q||_infinity<=3 and P(Q in I)<=3|I|.

next_action: Use the exact Schur-star ledger plus the opposite-sign Schur block to compile the quantitative tiny-H survivor into a source-coordinate mixed frame, grouped crossing/volume receiver, or bounded physical core before selecting an individual pair. The exact H=0 branch is block-diagonal on the same-sign Schur coordinates; approximate tiny-H cannot be treated perturbatively under arbitrary unbounded cap-one laws.
